text:
maya (Product): ok folks — we need to lock the SLO/scope for the fallback-routing MVP. customer asks + infra limits are colliding. quick take: p95 latency target 300ms for hosted, automatic fallback to 'small' model on queue/backpressure, and an error-budget policy. thoughts?

sam (Eng): 300ms p95 is tight but doable for short prompts. main impact is KV-cache fragmentation if we route across model families. implementing fallback routing + consistent cache keying ~ 2-3 sprints. can we relax p95 for initial rollout?

toni (SRE): relaxing p95 helps. my bigger worry is error-budget accounting: if fallback triggers a surge in errors/latency we need to avoid cascading. recommend a circuit-breaker that stops fallback after X% error budget burn in window and a per-tenant opt-out. also need synthetic checks for each model variant.

leila (Research): acceptance criteria must include quality regression checks for fallback model. propose: on our evaluation suites, fallback responses must have >= 0.92 ROUGE/embedding-similarity vs primary for the 80% of prompts that matter. edge case: hallucination rate must not increase by > 2x.

ricardo (CS): major enterprise customers asked for a per-tenant toggle today — they want fallback disabled for regulated tenants. this is a hard stop for some deals. +1 to per-tenant opt-out.

maya (Product): ok — proposal to reconcile: MVP scope = host-level fallback with default routing policy + metrics; per-tenant opt-out as a gated follow-up (prod week 2). launch criteria: 1) p95 <= 350ms on canary, 2) automated quality regression tests pass, 3) fallback circuit-breaker in prod, 4) monitoring dashboard + alerting.

sam (Eng): agree on compromise. will aim for p95 300ms in test, accept 350ms for canary. implementation notes: we add routing layer that maps request -> {primary_model, fallback_model, cache_key_prefix}, and fallback only if primary returns >500ms or 5xx. small config example: 

```json
{
  "service": "text.generate",
  "slo": { "latency_p95_ms": "300", "allowable_p95_ms_canary": "350" },
  "fallback": { "trigger_ms": "500", "fallback_model": "redwood-small-quant", "max_consecutive_fallbacks": "3" }
}
```

toni (SRE): +1. add these monitoring acceptance points to the PRD: 
- synthetic check every 1m per region per model variant
- error-budget burn alert at 25%/50%/90% thresholds
- automatic disable of fallback for a tenant after 2x baseline error rate for 10m
deploy-bot: PR opened — https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/452 (draft). CI: unit tests ok, e2e pending.

leila (Research): will run the fallback-quality harness against the top 500 customer prompts. acceptance: mean embedding-similarity >= 0.92 and hallucination delta <= 2x. will post results into the RFC thread.

maya (Product): owners: sam = eng owner, toni = SLO/runbooks, leila = quality gate, ricardo = customer opt-out policy. please add final acceptance criteria to RFC by EOD Thursday. prioritization note: if per-tenant opt-out requires schema changes, move to follow-up.

ricardo (CS): noted. I'll draft a simple policy string for customer-config UX: `fallback: enabled|disabled|force-primary`. will share sample tenant policy and legal checklist.

sam (Eng): one more edge-case: model-variant stateful sessions — we should avoid switching mid-session unless explicit. add rule: no fallback after user streaming start. small change but important.

maya (Product): good catch. add to acceptance: no mid-stream fallback. final ask: can we get a canary plan (region + 10% traffic) and a rollback playbook? toni + sam, can you write that into the RFC?

toni (SRE): will add canary + rollback steps and runbook snippets. sample alert text for ops: `SERVICE FallbackErrorBudgetBurn - > 50% in 10m - disable fallback for affected tenants`

maya (Product): thanks — if folks are aligned I'll move this into RFC review and tag stakeholders. pushing to ship MVP next quarter but want the SLO/rollback pieces firm first. :thumbsup:
